pages.text: Bram: $(italic)This one's a problem, not a recipe. Read the numbers, then build to them.$()$(br2)$(bold)Q71: hold 1,800 RPM under load, and do not go over.$()$(br2)The vessel payout is the crate: $(bold)64$() Turbine Casing, $(bold)16$() Turbine Glass, a Rotor Bearing, $(bold)4$() Shafts, $(bold)16$() Blades, $(bold)2$() Fluid Ports, $(bold)16$() copper blocks for the coil ring, and the Turbine Terminal to read it on. Spending all of it is not the answer, and nothing is lost by taking a piece back out.
pages.title: Eighteen hundred

pages.text: $(li)More $(bold)rotor blades$() -- more torque, slower spin.$(li)More $(bold)coils$() -- more power drawn, slower spin.$(li)More $(bold)steam$() -- faster spin.$(br2)So: build it, open the flow, read the RPM. Over 1,800, add a blade or a coil. Under, take one out. It settles in about three passes and there is no way to break it.
pages.title: How the three dials work

pages.text: $(bold)/valley check turbine$() prints RPM, steam in and power out without you opening a single menu. (Press $(bold)T$(), type it, press enter.)$(br2)Smallest turbine the game will accept: $(bold)5 x 5 x 4$().$(br2)Q83 asks for a second one that meets the town's stated winter budget without going past the fuel burn Tobin signed off. $(bold)/valley check power$() is the other half of that answer.
